algorithm_description: The algorithm updates x_{k+1} = prox_{eta*g}(x_k - eta * grad(f)(x_k)). Proof must utilize the non-expansiveness of the proximal operator.

--- judge_0 (openai/gpt-oss-120b, JRS=-0.566) ---
The manuscript states the ergodic convergence rate O(1/k) (Theorem \ref{thm:rate}) correctly (Dimension A). Assumption (A1) (L‑smoothness) is used in the descent lemma (Step 1) and applied correctly. Assumption (A3) (stepsize bound) is invoked in Step 8 and is correct. Assumption (A2) (convexity of g and existence of prox) is referenced in Lemma \ref{lem:nonexp} and later in Step 9, but the usage in Step 9 is flawed: the non‑expansiveness of the proximal operator is applied to the pair \(y_k, x^*\) instead of \(y_k, x^* - \eta\nabla f(x^*)\). The proof omits the crucial fixed‑point property \(x^* = \prox_{\eta g}(x^* - \eta\nabla f(x^*))\) that follows from optimality; this omission constitutes a missing logical step (Dimension C, Step 9). Consequently the inequality (S20) is incorrect, and all subsequent derivations (S21–S30) that rely on it are invalid. This also represents an operator‑error (misuse of the proximal operator) and a violation of Assumption (A2) (Dimension B, Step 9). Other parts of the proof are algebraically correct, but the central telescoping argument does not hold without the proper fixed‑point justification. No stochastic or expectation arguments are present, so no issues there. Overall the exposition is complete in terms of structure, but the core convergence argument is incomplete and mathematically unsound, leading to a moderate completeness score and assumption‑use score. The proof can be repaired by (i) explicitly stating and using the optimality condition \(0\in\nabla f(x^*)+\partial g(x^*)\) to obtain the fixed‑point relation, (ii) applying non‑expansiveness to the correct pair, and (iii) simplifying the resulting inequality to the standard bound \(\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|^2 \le \|x_k-x^*\|^2 - 2\eta(F(x_k)-F(x^*))\). After these corrections the ergodic O(1/k) rate follows directly.
